posts.name: 40-world-shroud-turin-dna
posts.caption:
Scientists sequenced the DNA on the Shroud of Turin and found mostly modern traces: the man who sampled it, dogs, cats, chickens, carrots and peanuts 🧬

The threads were taken in 1978. Most human DNA matched that collector, and plants like peanuts and corn only reached Europe after 1492. The authors say DNA cannot date the cloth. Two repair threads from its case dated to 1451 to 1622 and 1642 to 1800.

Source: Barcaccia, Rambaldi Migliore, Gabelli et al. (University of Padova, University of Pavia), “DNA signatures preserved in the official 1978 sample collection of the Shroud of Turin”, Scientific Reports, 2026.
